rationale: Drainage floor is a SAFETY constraint. It must hold regardless of enzyme performance or pulsation optimization. Frozen as a hard constraint.

minimum_drainage_rate_ml_min.tolerance: hard floor — never below this in any operating mode
minimum_drainage_rate_ml_min.rationale: Below 0.10 mL/min, CSF accumulates faster than it drains. ICP rises. Patient at risk of herniation within hours. This is a NON-NEGOTIABLE safety constraint that overrides any clearance optimization.

fail_safe_mode.trigger: If controller cannot maintain Q >= 0.10 mL/min due to enzyme membrane occlusion or valve malfunction
fail_safe_mode.action: Bypass enzyme membrane entirely. Direct drainage through passive pressure-reactive valve (standard shunt behavior). Patient loses clearance function but retains drainage. Same as standard of care.
fail_safe_mode.rationale: Drainage is life-critical. Clearance is therapeutic. Cannot trade life-critical for therapeutic.

alarm_threshold.Q_below_0.15_ml_min_for_5_min: Yellow alarm — notify patient, schedule replacement
alarm_threshold.Q_below_0.10_ml_min_for_60_sec: Red alarm — system enters fail-safe bypass mode, patient seek immediate medical attention

constitutional_basis: Article XXVII — threshold has explicit class (SAFETY / PHYSIOLOGICAL) and explicit justification. Cannot be silently relaxed.
relationship_to_P-01: P-01's INV-1 (P_ICP in [5, 20] mmHg) is the equivalent safety constraint. P-04's drainage floor is the local version: P-04 cannot cause P-01 to violate INV-1.
